evidence_requirements.statement: The scheduler reconciles desired graph state into a deterministic legal frontier without lifecycle choreography.
Hard, ordering-only, artifact, review, verification, and resource constraints are enforced with bounded shared/exclusive concurrency.
One primary writer per write worktree and persistent isolated WorkUnit workspace identity are enforced.
Stale work is detected and resume is idempotent with duplicate dispatch prevented.
Failures are classified and recovery retries are bounded, strategy/evidence aware, and escalated when policy requires.
Dispatch remains an adapter boundary and no automatic final landing or external effect is performed.
Deterministic simulated-adapter scheduler tests and a repository-local isolated progression smoke path pass.
Existing KEEL graph, lifecycle, authorization, worktree, and full regression checks remain passing.
The repository-local smoke path observes isolated WorkUnit progression across persisted resume without external effects.

non_goals: Do not implement a second generic agent runtime; Codex/runtime adapters remain the worker harness boundary.
Do not automatically land, merge, push, release, deploy, or perform external effects.
Do not replace canonical intent, ChangeGraph, evidence receipts, RuntimeProfile, CapabilityGrants, or existing safe integration semantics.
Do not add unbounded retries, speculative providers, or a fixed lifecycle choreography as orchestration authority.
objective: Implement desired-state reconciliation and bounded WorkUnit scheduling

requirements.statement: Implement a desired-state control loop that observes actual state, compares it with desired state, derives unmet conditions, computes a legal/runnable frontier, dispatches bounded actions through adapters, observes/classifies results, and can reconcile again without fixed lifecycle choreography.

Support hard dependency edges, supported ordering-only constraints, artifact/data dependencies, review/verification dependencies, resource claims, shared versus exclusive resources, bounded concurrency, one primary writer per write worktree, and safe read-heavy concurrency.
Persist isolated WorkUnit/workspace identity and enforce workspace ownership so work can resume idempotently and write worktrees have one primary writer.
Detect stale work and prevent duplicate dispatch, including when resuming persisted scheduler state.
Classify failures using the requested explicit classifications and apply bounded recovery; unchanged evidence and strategy must not cause infinite retries, and policy blockers must escalate.
Keep Codex as the worker harness and do not implement automatic final landing beyond existing safe integration semantics.
Provide deterministic simulated-adapter scheduler tests and at least one repository-local smoke path proving isolated WorkUnit progression without external effects.
Use existing KEEL governance and preserve canonical semantic, repository, evidence, runtime authorization, ledger, verification, commit, seal, integration, and anchor boundaries.
Provide repository-local smoke evidence that isolated WorkUnits progress and resume without external effects.

consequences: Scheduler mistakes could duplicate work, violate write isolation, or suppress runnable work.
Incorrect recovery classification could repeat failed actions or conceal authorization and specification blockers.
The control-plane boundary must remain compatible with existing canonical lifecycle, evidence, and worktree guarantees.
risk.review: Independent review must inspect scheduler invariants, adapter boundaries, persistence/isolation behavior, failure recovery, duplicate-dispatch prevention, and the complete deterministic regression evidence.

units.objective: Implement and verify the desired-state reconciler, bounded scheduler, simulated adapters, and isolated repository-local smoke path
